$comment: Rule catalog — monitoring. Standards 21, 22, 24. What happens after deployment: watching for shift, responding to it, and deciding when to retrain. Nothing here is machine-checkable from a repository — these are facts about a running system and the policies governing it — so every entry is attestation-only and says so.

rules.title: A response is defined for each drift threshold, with an owner
rules.description: Thresholds for input, output, and where possible outcome drift are defined before deployment, each with a stated response and a named owner.
rules.rationale: A threshold with no defined response produces an alert nobody acts on, and an alert nobody acts on trains everyone to ignore the next one. Defining the response before the first alert is also what prevents the threshold being revised upward the moment it fires.
rules.remediation: Write the thresholds, the response for each, and the owner, before deployment rather than after the first alert.
rules.evidenceExpected: A drift-monitoring specification listing metrics, thresholds, responses, and owners, plus an attestation that it is the one in force.
rules.$assuranceNote: Nothing automated establishes this. A document could be found; whether the thresholds are the ones configured in the running system, and whether anyone owns the response, cannot be seen from the repository.

rules.title: Evidence of distribution shift is not left unanswered
rules.description: Where monitoring or analysis indicates distribution shift, the finding must be acted on or explicitly dispositioned with a reason. Observing shift and continuing unchanged, without recording a decision, is this prohibition.
rules.rationale: Evidence of shift is information that obligates action, not a metric to be watched. The failure mode is not ignorance but inertia: the signal is seen, nothing is decided, and the absence of a decision is indistinguishable afterwards from never having looked.
rules.remediation: Record a disposition for each shift finding — retrain, adjust, accept with a reason, or escalate — with a date and an owner.
rules.evidenceExpected: A record of shift findings and their dispositions, and an attestation that no finding was left undispositioned.
rules.$assuranceNote: Nothing automated establishes this. It concerns what was decided in response to a production signal, which leaves no trace in the code.

rules.title: A written retraining policy exists before retraining is automated
rules.description: A retraining policy states its trigger, the data window it uses, the evaluation the new model must pass before replacing the old one, and the rollback path — and exists before retraining runs without a human in the loop.
rules.rationale: Automatic retraining with no evaluation gate propagates a data problem into production faster than a person could notice it. The gate is the whole value of the policy; the schedule is the easy part.
rules.remediation: Write the policy, and make the evaluation gate a blocking step in the retraining pipeline rather than a report produced after promotion.
rules.evidenceExpected: A retraining policy document naming trigger, window, gate, and rollback, and an attestation that the pipeline enforces the gate.
rules.$assuranceNote: Nothing automated establishes this. Whether a pipeline actually blocks on its evaluation gate is a property of the deployment system, not of the repository.

rules.title: The deployed model is observable, and monitoring is segmented
rules.description: Prediction volumes and distributions, input health, latency and error rates, and — where outcomes arrive — realised performance are monitored in production, broken down by segment rather than only in aggregate.
rules.rationale: Aggregate health routinely conceals a population for which the model has stopped working. A model can hold its overall metric while failing completely for a segment that is small in the data and not small in consequence.
rules.remediation: Define the monitored signals and their segmentation, with thresholds, alerts, and owners, before deployment.
rules.evidenceExpected: A monitoring specification covering the signals and their segmentation, and an attestation that it is deployed and firing.
rules.$assuranceNote: Nothing automated establishes this. Monitoring is a property of the running system; a repository can hold a configuration file that describes monitoring nobody deployed.
